questions.text: Which three criteria must approved plastics satisfy under PD 1096 Section 1601?

options.text: Flame-spread rating of 225 or less, smoke density not greater than untreated wood, and combustion products no more toxic than untreated wood
Flame-spread rating of 75 or less, ASTM label, and imported certification
Compressive strength, color stability, and UV warranty
Manufacturer reputation, recycled content, and warranty period

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Flame-spread rating of 225 or less, smoke density not greater than untreated wood, and combustion products no more toxic than untreated wood. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1601.

questions.text: What must be submitted for plastic materials under PD 1096 Section 1602?

options.text: Technical data establishing stresses, maximum unsupported spans, and other necessary information
Only a color sample
Only a brand brochure
Only a verbal installer assurance

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Technical data establishing stresses, maximum unsupported spans, and other necessary information. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1602.

questions.text: Under the 2004 DPWH Revised IRR, which plastic doors are not allowed for Group A to I occupancies?

options.text: Entrance doors and exit doors
Interior cabinet doors only
Nonrated wardrobe doors only
Temporary sample doors only

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Entrance doors and exit doors. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1603.
questions.explanation: The 3.00 m property line setback and 2.50 m lateral unit separation are two distinct spatial requirements that must both be applied on a roof layout. The lateral separation (2.50 m) is less commonly memorized than the property line setback (3.00 m), making this a high-difficulty paired-value question.

questions.text: For plastic skylights, what property-line setback applies except in Group A occupancies?

options.text: No skylight within 3.00 meters of a property line
No skylight within 300 millimeters of a property line
No skylight within 1.00 meter of a property line
No property-line setback is stated

questions.rationale: Correct answer: No skylight within 3.00 meters of a property line. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1604.
questions.explanation: The three-part AND condition is the foundation of the plastics approval framework. The wood benchmark for smoke and toxicity is a comparative standard — the plastic must perform no worse than wood on these parameters while also meeting the absolute ≤225 flame-spread limit.

questions.text: What lateral and slope separation is required between plastic skylights?

options.text: At least 2.50 meters laterally and 3.00 meters along the roof slope
At least 600 mm laterally and 1.20 meters vertically
At least 1.50 meters in any direction
No separation is required if plastic is approved

questions.rationale: Correct answer: At least 2.50 meters laterally and 3.00 meters along the roof slope. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1604.
questions.explanation: The standard (1st storey) versus exception (10.00 m outside highly restrictive zones) pairing is the primary testable fact of Sec. 1608. The zone-dependency of the exception — not sprinklers — is the key discriminator.

questions.text: What is the maximum area of an individual plastic skylight?

options.text: 10.00 square meters
15.00 square meters
20 percent of roof area without unit limit
600 millimeters square

questions.rationale: Correct answer: 10.00 square meters. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1604.
questions.explanation: The absolute prohibition on plastic in entrance/exit doors is a bright-line safety rule. It appears on the LEA as a scenario where the designer asks whether the prohibition can be waived — the answer is always no.

questions.text: What aggregate-area limit applies to plastics in skylights, monitors, and sawtooth glazing?

options.text: Not more than 20 percent of the floor area of the room or occupancy sheltered
Not more than 50 percent of exterior wall area
Not more than 10 percent of site area
No aggregate limit is stated

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Not more than 20 percent of the floor area of the room or occupancy sheltered. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1604.
questions.explanation: The 100 mm curb requirement is slope-triggered: it applies only when slope < 1:4. The slope threshold (1:4) must be recognized as the condition that activates the curb requirement. Steeper roofs have this requirement waived because gravity drainage prevents water accumulation.

questions.text: What curb requirement applies to plastic skylights on roofs with slope less than 1 in 3?

options.text: A 100 mm high curb, unless the specified wire screen alternative is provided
A 300 mm high curb in all cases
A 25 mm high curb only
No curb is ever required

questions.rationale: Correct answer: A 100 mm high curb, unless the specified wire screen alternative is provided. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1604.
questions.explanation: The 15.00 sq.m standard and the 22.50 sq.m relaxed limit are paired calculation values. The +50% multiplier is consistent with how the Code expresses zone-based relaxations. Calculating 15.00 × 1.50 = 22.50 should be automatic.

questions.text: For monitors and sawtooth roofs, what is the maximum area of individual plastic glazing?

options.text: 15.00 square meters
10.00 square meters
600 millimeters square
No unit area limit is stated

questions.rationale: Correct answer: 15.00 square meters. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1605.
questions.explanation: The 45 m unprotected / 30 m suppressed pairing is counter-intuitive: the suppressed case allows closer placement (30 m) than the unprotected case (45 m). This reflects that suppression compensates for fire exposure, enabling buildings to use plastic glazing closer to property lines than would otherwise be permitted.

questions.text: How must plastic light-transmitting panels in monitors and sawtooth roofs be separated?

options.text: By incombustible material or roofing material at least 1.50 meters long
By timber blocking at least 100 mm long
Only by sealant
No separation is needed

questions.rationale: Correct answer: By incombustible material or roofing material at least 1.50 meters long. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1605.
questions.explanation: The Types III/IV/V permission — excluding I and II — is a direct memory item. The underlying logic is that the more combustible construction types cannot safely combine with a plastic roof element. Remembering 'three through five' avoids confusing this with other Code provisions.

questions.text: What lower-edge condition applies to plastic panels in monitors and sawtooth roofs?

options.text: The lower edge must be at least 150 mm above the adjoining roof surface
The lower edge must touch the roof surface
The lower edge must be below the roof surface
The Code gives only a color requirement

questions.rationale: Correct answer: The lower edge must be at least 150 mm above the adjoining roof surface. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1605.
questions.explanation: The two quantitative triggers — 10% of a 10 sq.m ceiling and 65°C/15-minute retention — are both testable. The 10% threshold is assessed per the defined 10 sq.m reference room, not per the actual room area. The thermal retention requirement ensures diffusers do not become falling burning hazards.

questions.text: When must ceiling light diffusers be approved plastics under PD 1096 Section 1606?

options.text: When the diffuser area is greater than 10 percent of any 10.00 sq m room area
Whenever the diffuser is any size at all
Only when installed outdoors
Only when located in a greenhouse

questions.rationale: Correct answer: When the diffuser area is greater than 10 percent of any 10.00 sq m room area. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1606.
questions.explanation: The individual (10.00 sq.m) and aggregate (20% of floor area) limits are a paired set that both apply simultaneously. Satisfying one does not satisfy the other. The 20% aggregate is commonly confused with the 1/3 penthouse area limit — they are distinct provisions.

questions.text: What heat-detachment condition is stated for plastic light diffusers?

options.text: They must not readily become detached at room temperature of 80 C for 15 minutes, subject to stated exceptions
They must melt at 40 C
They must be removable by hand
They have no installation condition

questions.rationale: Correct answer: They must not readily become detached at room temperature of 80 C for 15 minutes, subject to stated exceptions. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Section 1606.

options.text: Where partitions are not required to be fire-resistive or incombustible construction
In all fire-resistive partitions without review
Only in exit doors
Only in exterior veneer

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Where partitions are not required to be fire-resistive or incombustible construction. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1607.

options.text: It shall not be attached above the first storey, subject to the stated exception outside highly restrictive fire zones
It may always reach any height
It is limited only by color
It is allowed only underground

questions.rationale: Correct answer: It shall not be attached above the first storey, subject to the stated exception outside highly restrictive fire zones. This is directly supported by PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Section 1608.

options.text: Not in excess of 10.00 meters above adjacent grade elevation

options.text: 1.20 meters vertically and 600 mm horizontally

options.text: Plastic materials appropriate for use according to flame-spread characteristics may be used if projections and appendages provisions are followed

options.text: Greenhouses in less restrictive fire zones
Exit doors in all occupancies

questions.text: Which statement best distinguishes Section 1601 approval from later installation limits?

options.text: Section 1601 defines approved plastic fire-performance criteria; later sections still control where and how approved plastics may be installed
Once plastic is approved under Section 1601, no other limits apply
Installation limits apply only to glass, not plastic
Only manufacturer warranty controls installation

questions.rationale: Correct answer: Section 1601 defines approved plastic fire-performance criteria; later sections still control where and how approved plastics may be installed. This is directly supported by PD 1096, Sections 1601-1609.
